name: Foreground occluder pass

source.description: 1 inspected reference film (batch-3, 2026-11-26): a transformation reel hides a morph behind a large blurred ring sweeping across the lens.

technique: A large, heavily blurred object sweeps across the lens for a few frames while the subject changes form behind it. The occluder hides the change and adds depth, like a camera passing a foreground object.
purpose: Hide a morph or state change and add depth, like a camera passing a foreground object.
visual_behaviour: A huge, heavily blurred object crosses the frame in a quarter second; behind it the subject has changed form.
mechanics: Foreground element 1.5-3x the frame height, blur 20-40 px, opacity 0.6-0.9, crossing the frame in 0.2-0.3 s (ref-19cee08f9c 4.12-4.35 s, 30 fps strip); swap or morph the subject while it is covered; move the occluder against the camera's direction.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Occluder height relative to the frame

use_cases: Hiding a morph or a state change
A softer alternative to a cut
failure_modes: A sharp occluder reads as an object in the scene, not a lens pass
Large blur filters cost raster time

implementation.approach: A top-layer shape 1.5-3x the frame height, CSS blur 20-40 px, opacity 0.6-0.9, crossing in 0.2-0.3 s against the camera's direction (Studio.fx.smear for the motion); swap or morph the subject while covered; land the strongest accent on the pass. Not built as a component.

provenance.observed: A large blurred ring sweeps across the lens in about 0.23 s while chrome rings close into a sphere cage behind it; the strongest accent of that stretch lands at 4.27 s.

licensing_notes: Technique only, learned from user-supplied references (inspiration-only, rights unknown).
